chapter: Arranging for other bandleaders and closing talk
title: Taking gigs and Minton's sessions for fresh ideas while arranging
summary: While arranging in New York he played occasional gigs and one-nighters with Dizzy Gillespie and Joe Guy, jotting riffs in a notebook; he may still have the notebooks.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: No, I was just writing at that time. Every now and then, being in New York, you know, a few gigs would come up, and I'd take them, just enough to be able to gather new ideas, you know. I would wanted to be around guys, and like those jam sessions at Minton's, you know. Sometimes they

would need a piano player, you know, one of those things, and I would take the thing, man, just to hear what I'd been missing, you know, from certain guys, and I would hear some great things, you know, and I'd remember those things, and in my next arrangement I used to include some of those things, you know, because I always carried my little notebook with me, you know, and those little riffs that they'd make and some hard things. And some of these guys that did some of these things -- the great Dizzy Gillespie, of course, and he was full of ideas, you know. Great trumpet player, Joe Guy -- I did a lot of dates, single dates with these guys, and we'd go as far as up in Massachusetts, you know, play a one nighter and come back. They'd have a 12 piece band, you know.
We had that gig book, you know. It was simplified--
Because you didn't have a chance . . . . But

It kind of kept the thing from getting monotonous, you know, writing all the time, you know. It kind of kept your fingers a little nimble, you know. Of course, as I said before, you'd always find somebody that played something that you could use, a little bit here, a little group there, you know.
I think I asked you this before.
Do you still have any of those notebooks?
Somewhere around here, I don't know. I don't know if anybody could make heads or tails out of these, except for me.
It would be interesting to see one of those sometimes.
Well, I'll have to dig up one or two for you.
